usage: 1. n8n → Workflows → Import from File, select this file.
2. Create a generic 'Header Auth' credential named 'SocialCRM Cron': name=x-cron-secret, value=<the same value as CRON_SECRET in the target env>.
3. Set the n8n env var SOCIALCRM_BASE_URL (e.g. https://app.yourdomain.com), or replace the URL expressions with a literal.
4. Both HTTP nodes already reference the 'SocialCRM Cron' credential — open each and confirm it is selected.

5. Dry run: disable the Schedule Trigger, click 'Execute Workflow' once, confirm GET → Split Out → POST produces one POST per waiting lead (2xx on each: 201 created / 200 duplicate|not_waiting). Then enable the schedule.

NOTE: If your n8n already auto-splits a top-level JSON array into items, the 'Split Out Leads' node is redundant — delete it and connect 'Get Waiting Leads' → 'Create Recovery Alert' directly. Quick check: a single GET execution shows N output items (auto-split) vs 1 item containing the array (needs Split Out).
SUCCESS CODES: 201 (created), 200 (duplicate | not_waiting) are all success and expected. 403 = bad/expired credential; 400 = bad body; 500 = secret unset on the server.

parameters.content:
## Recovery Alerts intake
Schedule (10m) → GET waiting leads → split → POST create-recovery-alert.

Auth: Header Auth credential 'SocialCRM Cron' (x-cron-secret = CRON_SECRET).
Base URL: env SOCIALCRM_BASE_URL.

201 created / 200 duplicate|not_waiting = success.
Duplicate prevention is enforced server-side (one open alert per lead), so overlapping runs are safe.
